I used to have dark blonde hair, now at 18 I have dark brown.
ELI5: why does hair darken as we age?

The amount of melanin - a natural pigmentation - in the hair strands is what dictates the color. There are two types of melanin in hair, eumelanin and pheomelanin. Eumelanin controls the darkness; the more of it, the darker the hair and vice versa. Pheomelanin controls the redness; the more of it, the redder the hair and vice versa.

The level of each type is controlled by certain genes being on or off, therefore the color of hair is based on the expression of these genes. The expression of these genes is not constant during life, which leads to changes in hair color. The most common change is an increase in eumelanin (hence, darkening) through childhood. The reason that the genes change expression is not understood.

I think it has something to do with the fact that you aren't used to seeing your face not reflected in a mirror. Also, when you look at a mirror you make a face that you can see looks good. When you are taking a picture you just have to try and make a face you think looks good.

You judge yourself from one perspective if you see your reflection, so your mind finishes the picture with assumptions. So if you see yourself in a picture you compare it to the image you have of yourself, and since it looks nothing like it. And based on this it looks really wrong for you, however if you take an image that looks similar to poses you can have in reflections, it will look fine to you.

It is like you expect yourself to be A and you look like B, and instead of comparing yourself to other people, you compare yourself to a better looking version you thought you were. Similar happens when you hear your own voice. After looking at enough pictures and enough footage, you should become more open minded, and appreciate yourself more.
